findings.evidence:
YouTubeAccessibilityGuideDialog.kt:42-83 explains restricted-settings bypass and enabling service, but does not explain event/package data access, processing or sharing, and :109-116 opens Accessibility Settings without affirmative data-use consent. XML :6 enables canRetrieveWindowContent=true despite service :14-26 using only packageName for deterministic YouTube launch detection. isAccessibilityTool is absent. No screen-text or keystroke collection/upload observed.

**Critic Verification**: Guide dialog supplies restricted-settings instructions and direct accessibility-settings navigation, without an affirmative data-use consent gate or an explanation of package/window event access. XML enables window-content retrieval although the service only reads event.packageName. This confirms the concrete disclosure/minimization gap, without assuming any screen text upload. (Confidence: High)
findings.issue_summary: Accessibility setup lacks prominent data-use disclosure and affirmative consent
findings.recommendation: Prefer manual operation or narrower API. If keeping the deterministic listener, disable window-content retrieval, provide separate prominent disclosure of package/window-event access and local use/sharing, require explicit consent before settings navigation, and complete the Play Accessibility declaration and listing disclosure. Do not mark this general wellness utility as a disability accessibility tool.

findings.evidence:
YouTubeDetectionAccessibilityService.kt:21-26 invokes startForegroundService directly on package detection. Manifest :173-176 declares camera type. EyeExerciseOverlayService.kt:299-304 starts foreground notification then camera. AccessibilityService's background-start allowance does not itself establish the separate camera while-in-use exemption; this event-triggered path has no visible activity/user notification interaction.

**Critic Verification**: YouTubeDetectionAccessibilityService directly calls startForegroundService on a package event, without visible-Activity interaction. Manifest declares camera FGS and EyeExerciseOverlayService.onCreate immediately starts foreground mode and setupCameraX. This confirms an unsupported camera-start path needing remediation; accessibility-related background-start permission does not establish a camera while-in-use exception. No off-device transmission is inferred. (Confidence: High)
findings.issue_summary: YouTube listener starts camera FGS from background without a demonstrated while-in-use exemption
findings.recommendation: Replace automatic camera startup with a user-visible prompt that opens the app; start a session from its visible Activity with CAMERA granted. Verify both background-start and camera while-in-use requirements independently and handle denial/revocation without crash.
